settings.colour_note: Prefer black parts. A black version of the same model at the same or lower landed cost replaces the pick; black options that cost more or change the spec are suggested with reason 'colour'.

fit_limits.notes: GPU length is 435mm without front fans; the two 25mm front fans make it about 410mm. 95mm = card thickness + bottom fan: Jonsbo quotes 117mm from the top slot, but the Mortar's x16 slot may sit one slot lower, so 95mm is used to be safe. PSU 160mm = the ATX front bay (an ATX PSU leaves room for 2×120mm front fans). The top takes a 240 or 360mm radiator. With an AIO there's no air-cooler limit on RAM; kits up to 43mm clear the radiator. Case fans: 3 bottom, 2 front, 1 rear; the top three mounts hold the radiator fans. Air-cooler limit if ever swapped: 172mm.

suggestions.name: ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 XT OC 16GB
suggestions.why: The same RX 9070 XT chip and 16GB as the Reaper, in ASUS's black Prime OC with a slightly higher factory clock, sold by Amazon UK with free delivery. It is 312mm long and 50mm thick, so it clears the D33 and the bottom fans (75mm of 95mm). Trade-off: it takes three 8-pin power plugs instead of two, so check the PSU's PCIe leads.

suggestions.name: Gigabyte Radeon RX 9070 XT Gaming OC 16GB
suggestions.why: Same RX 9070 XT chip and 16GB in Gigabyte's black triple-fan Gaming OC, sold by Amazon UK with free delivery (Computer Orbit lists it at £699 but it's out of stock). At 288mm long and 56mm thick it fits the D33 and the bottom fans (81mm of 95mm). Trade-off: a thicker card with three 8-pin plugs, and ASUS's Prime is a little cheaper.

suggestions.name: MSI MAG A850GL PCIE5 850W Gold, fully modular
suggestions.why: MSI's black 850W Gold PSU: fully modular, ATX 3 with a native 12V-2x6 cable, 140mm long so it fits the D33 like the RM850e, with the same 7-year warranty. Sold by Amazon UK at £89.99 with free delivery now that Amazon's own RM850e listing has gone and other shops want £119+. Trade-off: rated 80 Plus Gold rather than Cybenetics Gold, and reviews put it a touch louder under heavy load.

suggestions.name: ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 XT OC 16GB
suggestions.why: The same RX 9070 XT chip and 16GB as the Reaper, in ASUS's black Prime OC with a slightly higher factory clock, sold by Amazon UK with free delivery. It is 312mm long and 50mm thick, so it clears the D33 and the bottom fans (75mm of 95mm). Trade-off: it takes three 8-pin power plugs instead of two, so check the PSU's PCIe leads.

suggestions.name: Sapphire Pulse Radeon RX 9070 XT 16GB
suggestions.why: The same RX 9070 XT chip and 16GB as the Reaper in Sapphire's black triple-fan Pulse, sold by Amazon UK at £825.99 with free delivery, about £74 under the Reaper now it has risen to £899.99. At 320mm long and 61.6mm thick it fits the D33 and clears the bottom fans (87mm of 95mm), and uses two 8-pin plugs like the Reaper. Trade-off: a chunkier 3-slot card than the slim 2-slot Reaper, with less spare room above the bottom fans.

suggestions.name: XFX Swift Radeon RX 9070 XT Triple Fan Gaming 16GB, black (RX-97TSWF3B9)
suggestions.why: XFX's black triple-fan RX 9070 XT: the same chip and 16GB as the Reaper, £839.99 at Scan (in stock, low stock), about £47 under the Reaper's £899.99 even after Scan's £13.19 NI delivery. At 325mm long and 65mm thick it fits the D33 and clears the bottom fans (90mm of 95mm), with two 8-pin plugs like the Reaper and an 850W PSU minimum, which the RM850e meets. Trade-off: a 3.5-slot card, the tightest fit above the bottom fans of any option so far, and s7 is still about £14 cheaper.

upgrades.name: AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D (8 cores)
upgrades.why: Two more cores: faster in CPU-heavy games (BG3's Act 3, strategy, sims). At 4K on the TV the graphics card is usually the limit, so it's the upgrade to make only if the budget stretches.

upgrades.name: WD Black SN7100 2TB (TLC, PCIe 4.0)
upgrades.why: TLC flash: faster sustained writes and much higher endurance than the QLC Crucial. Nice to have, not needed for a games drive.

upgrades.name: Thermalright Peerless Vision 360 ARGB, black (3.95" 480×480 LCD)
upgrades.why: Same 397mm radiator, a bigger 3.95in square screen on the pump, and a few pounds cheaper at Computer Orbit. Different pump look from the photo, so it's your call.

upgrades.name: PowerColor Radeon RX 9070 XT Hellhound 16GB
upgrades.why: Same chip and speed with a bigger, even quieter cooler. Only worth it if near-silence matters more than the extra cost.
